text:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU OOM on cluster-prod-3 during prefill. 25% of containers on node g3-14 restarted in last 2m. Paging oncall.

incident-bot: Pager routed to @sara-oncall (SRE rotation).

sara-oncall: seeing the alert, grabbing context. Any customer impact reported yet? :eyes:

mike-sre: looking at node g3-14 logs now. early signs point to very large prefill sequences + kvcache pressure. getting repeated `CUDA out of memory` in container runtime.

ana-ml-runtime: FYI that model group has long-context clients right now (some sessions ~180k tokens). Prefill loop tries to allocate kv cache at once; we saw streaming prefill earlier but not this magnitude.

sara-oncall: can you paste tail of the crash log?

mike-sre: here are the last few lines from the kube logs:

```
2026-02-18T03:12:07Z model-runtime[pid:8421]: Allocating KV cache 48GB
2026-02-18T03:12:07Z model-runtime[pid:8421]: GPU 0: CUDA error: out of memory
2026-02-18T03:12:07Z model-runtime[pid:8421]: Container exit code 137
2026-02-18T03:12:08Z kubelet: restarting container model-server-.. on g3-14
```

ana-ml-runtime: that's consistent. we also pulled a GPU trace: `cuMemAlloc` failures during prefill-kv-map.

ana-ml-runtime: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) drain node g3-14 to stop new prefills 2) enforce prefill token limit at the proxy for active sessions 3) route traffic for long sessions to coldmodel (lower VRAM variant)

sara-oncall: I'll cordon+drain the node. evan-custops can you prepare a customer-facing blurb if this affects latency?

ev an-custops: on it. any ETA on mitigation?

mike-sre: running: `kubectl cordon g3-14 && kubectl drain g3-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` now. stopping new pods from scheduling.

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered: enable-prefill-trimmer v1 -> prod (canary 5%). Triggered by sara-oncall.

sara-oncall: enabling proxy prefill limiter (max_prefill_tokens=20000) across edge proxies. This should reject extremely long single-message prefill requests with 413.

ana-ml-runtime: also toggle fallback routing: map requests with >32k tokens to coldmodel-xxl. Applying routing rule now.

mike-sre: node drained, evicted pods finishing restart on other nodes. Restarts decreasing. memory footprint on neighbors stable so far.

sara-oncall: good. starting a 15m watch. please add any anomalies to the thread.

ev an-custops: customer blurb draft: "We're investigating increased restarts for inferences with very large context windows. We're applying traffic controls to limit prefill size and routing very long sessions to lower-memory variants to restore stability. We'll follow up with impacted customers if we see errors or latency increases." Thoughts?

mike-sre: good. also recommend adding temporary sampling of offending request IDs for a postmortem. `kubectl logs --since=1h | grep -E "session_id|token_count"` gave many >120k tokens.

ana-ml-runtime: logging added, and we've enabled an automatic fallback: if `cuMemAlloc` fails, runtime will now trim prefix and attempt a fallback allocation path (coldmodel) to avoid SIGKILL. Hotpatch deployed to canary.

sara-oncall: roll the hotpatch to 20% after 10m of stable canary then to 100% if no regressions.

incident-bot: NOTE: page escalated to oncall-2 if error rate > 5% over 10m.

mike-sre: error rate peaked at 6.3% five minutes ago, now 1.2%. back to watch mode.

ev an-custops: sending initial note to customers who had >50k token requests in last 24h.

sara-oncall: summary for handoff: cordoned g3-14, drained and redistributed pods, enabled proxy prefill limiter (20k tokens), routed >32k sessions to coldmodel, deployed runtime fallback hotpatch (canary -> 20%), added request sampling. No confirmed data loss; partial latency impact for very long sessions.

ana-ml-runtime: follow-ups for next 72h: add server-side trimming policy for prefills, add quota per-session hard limits, improve KV allocation backoff behavior, long-term: KV sharding and streaming prefill.

mike-sre: closing pager for now. keep thread open for handoff.

sara-oncall: thanks all. next oncall please continue 1h watch. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> monitoring. Incident ID: INC-2026-0218-3189
